scope: Corollary 6.9 (The flat trace solution operator) of the manuscript “The nonmaximal anti-de Sitter Penrose Inequality and original-data rigidity” (preprints/The-nonmaximal-anti-de-Sitter-Penrose-Inequality-and-original-data-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e2b9ba2768918dc), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 72. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For fixed N ≥ 4, τ > 0, a finite ΩR, and any ξ ∈ [0, 4], the trace equation of Proposition 4.17 has a unique solution f = Sξ(Z) ∈ C3,b′ for every Z ∈ C1,b′ with zero outer value. It has the continuity and bounded-input estimates of Proposition 6.8, without a floor assumption.
